Hi Eli — thanks for the note and the attachments, very helpful. I pulled the sample row from your CSV and ran the same request through our debug metering pipeline; below is the step-by-step and a worked example. I'll also loop Marissa for formal reconciliation and potential one-off credits if anything looks off. Ben, FYI for the commercial side.

Short summary of our metering rules that apply to your sample:
1) Tokenization: We tokenize the entire payload (history + prompt + model output) using the model-specific tokenizer.
2) Context bucketization: For requests where the request history exceeds 8k tokens, we first apply an internal "context windowing" step: the runtime keeps a rolling active window (8k tokens default for long-history paths) for latency SLOs. Any tokens outside the active window are not sent to the model but are still represented in the KV cache bookkeeping. Billing treats those as "inactive-history" tokens and applies a reduced-weight charge (currently 10% of full token unit).
3) Rounding quantum: We bill generation+context as follows — per-call tokens are summed, then rounded up to the nearest 50-token quantum for single-response calls. Streaming calls are rounded to the nearest 25-token quantum per streaming chunk boundary (we aggregate contiguous chunks within 1s when computing the quantum).
4) Minimum floor: There is a per-call minimum of 150 billed tokens for any non-zero call that invokes the model (this prevents extremely small spammy calls from fragmenting invoices). For customers on committed plans we apply a different floor calculation (see note).

Worked example (your sample request):
- Raw tokenization: history=7,200 tokens, prompt=420 tokens, output=2,600 tokens => raw total 10,220 tokens.
- Active window: runtime kept 8,000 tokens in the active window; the remaining 1,220 tokens are counted as inactive-history (charged at 10% weight): effective context charge = 8,000 + 0.1*1,220 = 8,122 tokens equivalent.
- Sum for metering before rounding: 8,122 (effective context) + 2,600 (output) = 10,722 tokens.
- Rounding (single-response): round up to nearest 50 -> 10,750 billed tokens.
- Apply per-call minimum: not applicable (above 150).

On the invoice we also show a separate line for "KV cache re-use credits" when a request reuses model keys within the same session: cache hits give a line-item credit (negative usage) when the reuse threshold is met; those credits are applied after raw metering but before tier/discount application.

Why this can look higher than expected: if you have many calls that partially reuse history but fall above the active window threshold, the inactive-history reduced-weight still contributes non-zero billing. Also, lots of short streaming chunks can hit the 25-token quantum repeatedly — that amplifies counts.

- Marissa, can you prepare an export that shows cache-credit line items for ELI-2026-0042 for April (I suspect a few credits did not apply automatically due to session id mismatch).

1) For the inactive-history reduced-weight, can you confirm whether that charge is shown as its own invoice line or rolled into the same generate+context line? Our accounting team only saw a single line and assumed everything was full-weight.
2) For streaming, we do have many 1–2s streamed responses; can you confirm the aggregation window (you mentioned 1s) — if a client streams 3 successive chunks spaced 0.8s apart, is that treated as one aggregated chunk for quantum rounding?
3) We're concerned about session id mismatches you noted — can you suggest the best practice to guarantee cache-credit visibility? We can switch to a session token header if that helps.

Also attaching a small CSV of two more sample requests (long_single.csv) and a short stream sample (stream_sample.csv) — please use those for the formal breakdown.

If the final line-item shows an unexpected delta after your breakdown we may open a procurement dispute; we'd appreciate Marissa's tally before we escalate.
